claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating can adhere effectively to a Cu matrix.
Applying an AlCoCrFeNi coating enhances the wear resistance of a Cu matrix.
Interfacial metallurgical bonds are responsible for the coating's effective adhesion and enhanced wear resistance.
The initial Cu matrix has a native oxide layer.
Thermal spraying or a similar deposition method can deposit an AlCoCrFeNi coating onto the Cu matrix.
Controlled thermal deposition conditions can permit limited interdiffusion without degrading the Cu substrate.
The AlCoCrFeNi coating and Cu substrate can be made compatible in thermal expansion under the proposed deposition conditions.
Partial interdiffusion promotes metallurgical bonding at the AlCoCrFeNi/Cu interface.
Thin intermetallic or solid-solution layers form at the AlCoCrFeNi/Cu interface.
An optimized deposition temperature causes limited interdiffusion between the AlCoCrFeNi coating and Cu substrate.
The resulting metallurgically bonded interface can accommodate mechanical stresses.
Accommodation of mechanical stresses by the interface increases adhesive strength.
Accommodation of mechanical stresses by the interface increases wear resistance.
The coated Cu substrate will have significantly greater wear resistance than uncoated Cu.
Uncoated Cu has lower wear resistance than the proposed AlCoCrFeNi-coated Cu.
An excessive thermal-expansion mismatch between the HEA coating and Cu may prevent effective adhesion.
Deposition-induced unwanted phases may compromise the coating/substrate interface.
The interface chemistry, phase formation, and degree of metallurgical bonding require experimental validation under specified deposition conditions.
